transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Notes: recording auto, mix of AE+SE from Redwood and netops/security from HelioPharm

Summary:
Quick status of onprem pilot bakeout. Reviewed kernel/quant patch results, p99 latency regressions in some cases, KV cache warm-up behavior, intermittent PSK handshake drop on one data center path, KMS/rotation impact on TLS sessions. Decided next steps: Redwood to ship patch+test recipe, customer to schedule maintenance window for controlled deploy and run 10k-rps canary, exchange security artifacts.

Topics:
- Kernel patch results and regressions
- VPC egress path and PSK handshake flakiness
- Telemetry and tracing gaps (missing token-level timing for some requests)
- KMS/HSM interactions and session persistence
- Rollout plan and risk handoff

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alyssa: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run 50 minutes or so, is that still good for you all?
[00:06] Tom Liang: yes that's fine, we have Elena and Sophia here from netops and security, Rajesh will jump in for the perf pieces.
[00:12] Rajesh: yeah, hi sorry late on my side, been looking at the numbers you sent this morning.
[00:18] Devon: cool, we'll start with the kernel patch results then go into the egress/handshake piece. quick reminder: patch was rolling quantization kernel and a small batching change.
[00:27] Elena: can you remind me what the patch touched? I skimmed the doc, saw kv-cache timing and a kernel rewrite for attention.
[00:33] Devon: right — attention microkernel path, plus a change to the continuous batching heuristic so it will flush at 48ms by default instead of 32ms under heavy concurrency. that was to reduce tokenization stalls we observed.
[00:45] Rajesh: from our afternoon tests p50 improved slightly, p95 about same, but p99 got worse in a small subset — 420ms -> 510ms on a few long-context requests, is that expected?
[00:56] Devon: hmm yeah so the quant path reorders a memory copy and that can push some long-sequence KV lookups into a slightly slower path when the cache is cold. we expected some warmup penalty but not at p99 that high.
[01:10] Alyssa: important to flag that the overall cost per token dropped in most loads, but we need to avoid tail latency for your user flows.
[01:18] Rajesh: the failing flows were mainly our EHR-parsing workload — long tokens, a lot of prefix reuse, so warm KV cache should help but we still saw spikes.
[01:27] Devon: ok, two things then: we have a follow-up micro-patch that changes the KV prefetch timing (reduces cold miss stalls) and a fallback config that forces fp16 for sequences over 2k tokens. We'll provide both.
[01:40] Elena: also, side note: when we ran from our colo in SJC the PSK handshake between our VPN concentrator and the private node dropped during the 2 sustained 5k tests. saw 12% handshake retries.
[01:52] Speaker 1: (murmur) did you capture tcpdump?
[01:55] Elena: yes, we forwarded a pcap, it's in the shared folder, file name psk-handshake-drop-0504.pcap.
[02:00] Devon: we saw that too on our side in the telemetry — the TLS session renegotiation is triggered by the KMS key rotation timing, and if the PSK gets rotated without session rekey handling the node drops.
[02:12] Sophia: is that because sessions are sticky to the old key? we have a short rotation period in prod, 6 hours, but can extend for pilot.
[02:19] Devon: correct, two interactions — KMS rotation causing TLS rekey and the kernel change altering the socket handling order. they collided in your tests.
[02:28] Tom: this is a concern for us, because our compliance requires key rotation. we won't accept a manual-only approach for production. what's the mitigation?
[02:36] Devon: plan is to add a small handshake backoff and session continuation patch so rekeys don't drop in-flight requests; alternative is to schedule KMS rotation outside heavy windows.
[02:46] Rajesh: what about telemetry, we saw missing spans for about 8% of requests during the test that had dropped p99 — makes root cause harder to trace.
[02:55] Maria: that's on us to add more tracer hooks, we can add token-level timestamps in the next build. but we need you to run the synthetic with the new tracer to validate.
[03:03] Alyssa: let's go through the risk matrix quickly, list of high/medium/low:
[03:08] Devon: high — p99 tail for EHR long context; high — PSK/KMS drop under rotation; medium — missing telemetry spans; low — minor cost delta when forcing fp16 fallback.
[03:17] Elena: for the PSK issue, we can also reconfigure our VPN to allow larger handshake windows, but that doesn't fix the underlying TLS rekey interaction.
[03:26] Sophia: we need to ensure the KMS policy we give you is minimal and audit-friendly. can you accept a read-only token scope for the pilot?
[03:33] Alyssa: yes we can. we'll accept read-only KMS access and support an HSM-backed key path if needed. we'll send a minimal example policy.
[03:41] Rajesh: about the quantization — if we force fp16 for >2k tokens will that blow up costs? we've got a lot of long job runs.
[03:50] Devon: small cost increase on those long sequences, but on average the per-token CPU/GPU utilization is lower, so unit cost is often still better than previous builds. it's workload dependent.
[03:59] Tom: do you have numbers? we need an estimate for the CFO team.
[04:03] Alyssa: I'll attach a pilot showback spreadsheet, with conservative and aggressive estimates — I'll send by EOD.
[04:10] Speaker 1: (interrupt) question on canary strategy — are we doing region-by-region or node-by-node?
[04:16] Devon: recommend node-by-node within the same AZ first, then a small region canary. we want to catch PSK handshake issues without impacting global traffic.
[04:24] Rajesh: ok, run 10k-rps for 15 minutes then step to 25k for 5, watch p99 and connection retry rates.
[04:32] Elena: for our maintenance window, can we do a rolling deploy 02:00-04:00 SJC? less traffic then.
[04:38] Tom: yes that's fine.
[04:40] Devon: good. We'll drop the patch and test recipe into the secure share; it will include exact curl/bench commands, and a script to toggle fp16 fallback.
[04:50] Alyssa: one more compliance note — we will provide the SOC2 artifact bundle and a short summary of the telemetry retention.
[04:56] Sophia: please include audit log retention periods, IP allowlist requirements, and full SAML flow details. we can't accept long-lived tokens.
[05:04] Maria: noted, we'll include SAML metadata for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and RBAC mapping examples.
[05:12] Rajesh: returning to perf quickly — can the kernel patch be toggled at runtime so we can A/B compare?
[05:18] Devon: yes it's a runtime flag, we can flip between old and new kernel on the same node for a short window, though you'll see some cache churn.
[05:26] Elena: that helps. we'll prefer toggling vs full deploy to reduce blast radius.
[05:31] Alyssa: recap of decisions: Redwood will ship kernel+kv prefetch micro-patch and a handshake backoff fix; provide test recipe and telemetry hooks; customer will schedule rolling maintenance for 2026-05-09 02:00-04:00 SJC; security will exchange KMS policy and SAML metadata; AE will send pricing and pilot showback.
[05:48] Tom: agreed, please add the known risks into the runbook.
[05:52] Alyssa: will do — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links. meeting adjourned.
